events.title: The Edict of Thessalonica
events.shortBlurb: The emperors declared the Nicene faith the religion of the Roman world, naming as its standard the creed held at Rome and Alexandria…
body: On 27 February 380 Theodosius I, newly baptized at Thessalonica by its bishop Ascholius, issued from that city the decree Cunctos populos in his own name and those of his colleagues Gratian and Valentinian II. It commanded all the peoples under their rule to hold the faith 'which the divine Apostle Peter delivered to the Romans', now professed by Pope Damasus and by Peter, bishop of Alexandria.

That faith the edict defined as belief in the single Godhead of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, in equal majesty and holy Trinity. Those who kept it were to be called Catholic Christians; the rest, adjudged 'demented and insane', were branded with the name of heretics, to suffer first the judgment of God and then the punishment of the imperial power.

The decree, preserved in the Theodosian Code, made the Nicene faith the religion of the Roman state after long decades of Arian ascendancy in the East. The next year Theodosius gathered the bishops in the First Council of Constantinople, which reaffirmed and enlarged the creed of Nicaea and sealed the triumph of the orthodox faith in the empire.
